## Top stories

- **Google DeepMind releases Genie 4 interactive world model:** Google DeepMind has launched Genie 4, a new world-generation model featuring real-time audio generation, text prompting during active simulations, and more realistic environmental rendering [TechCrunch AI]. The model is currently accessible in research preview to trusted testers to generate interactive experiences [The Verge AI].
- **Major Dhaka Metro contracts awarded to Indian firm L&T:** Indian engineering firm Larsen & Toubro (L&T) secured $1 billion in contracts for Dhaka Metro Rail, covering track works, electrical systems, signaling, telecommunications, and platform screen doors [The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour]. The overall development encompasses four construction packages that include an 11.5-kilometer rail line and eight stations [AmaderShomoy.com].
- **High university spending contrasted with 32% graduate unemployment in Bangladesh:** Government expenditure on higher education currently stands at Tk 13.5 lakh per university student annually [The Daily Campus]. Despite this significant state investment, official data highlights persistent labor market challenges, with 32% of graduates remaining unemployed [The Daily Campus].
- **GM ends century-long NYSE run to list on Nasdaq:** General Motors is shifting its public stock listing to the Nasdaq after spending more than a century on the New York Stock Exchange [NYT Business]. The strategic change aligns the traditional automotive giant closer with high-profile technology firms listed on the tech-heavy exchange [NYT Business].
- **Bangladesh and Japan explore $6.3 billion private investment framework:** Delegations from Bangladesh and Japan have held discussions regarding $6.3 billion in prospective private investment spanning energy, infrastructure, and ICT sectors [Prothom Alo English]. Concurrently, agreements have progressed regarding patrol vessels provided by Japan to bolster maritime security in Bangladesh [Just News BD].
- **Ransomware data recovery executive indicted for victim fraud:** The CEO of MonsterCloud, Zohar Pinhasi, has been indicted by US federal authorities for allegedly defrauding victims of ransomware attacks [Hacker News]. The charges detail fraudulent practices committed while purportedly performing data recovery operations for compromised entities [Hacker News].

---

## AI

- **Genie 4 world model debut:** Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, featuring real-time natural language prompts, realistic world generation, audio capabilities, and underlying Gemini integration in research preview [The Verge AI, TechCrunch AI].
- **Firefox introduces Smart Window AI enhancements:** Mozilla added intelligent form-filling capabilities to Firefox's Smart Window, enabling users to automatically populate application fields by drawing information from active tabs such as portfolios or LinkedIn [The Verge AI].
- **Meta AI leader departs to launch productivity startup:** Longtime Meta AI evaluations director Rohit Patel has left the company to launch Ndoc, an AI startup designed to compete with Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace [TechCrunch AI].
- **Anthropic faces scrutiny over Claude training data:** Reports revealed that AI developer Anthropic used illegally acquired books from Stanford University professors to train its Claude foundation models [Hacker News].
- **Critical reception of Elon Musk's AI movie:** Reviewers broadly criticized Elon Musk's newly released AI-generated film adaptation of *The Odyssey*, developed using Grok as an alternative to Christopher Nolan's cinematic project [The Guardian Business].

---

## Business

- **General Motors transfers to Nasdaq:** Automaker GM concluded more than 100 years on the NYSE to shift its equity listing to the Nasdaq exchange [NYT Business].
- **Honda cautions against proposed US auto tariffs:** Honda issued warnings that proposed 50% tariffs on Canadian auto imports threatened by Donald Trump would trigger catastrophic consequences for the integrated North American automotive supply chain [CNBC Business].
- **IDLC Finance posts 17% profit rise:** Financial institution IDLC Finance PLC reported a 17 percent increase in net profit to Tk 200 crore for the first nine months of 2026, driven by stronger operating revenues and investment returns [The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour].
- **JetBlue shares rally 20%:** JetBlue stock jumped significantly following an updated company outlook aimed at aggressive cost-cutting measures and expanded premium revenue offerings [CNBC Business].
- **Chinese intervention fails to arrest stock decline:** State-backed funds in China, known as the "national team," intervened in equity markets, though the domestic market continued to drop amid persistent investor skepticism [NYT Business].
- **Airlines lift rewards program costs:** American Airlines increased the annual cardholder fee on its primary co-branded credit card, marking its first fee bump since 2018 [CNBC Business].
- **UK minimum wage updates:** British officials confirmed an upcoming rise in the national minimum wage, though workers aged 18 to 20 will not be granted a larger proportional increase [BBC Business].

---

## Tech

- **Apple unveils 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by M6:** Apple officially introduced its updated 14-inch MacBook Pro lineup featuring the next-generation M6 processor [Hacker News].
- **Apple foldable phone reviewed:** Ars Technica reviewed Apple's dual-screen foldable iPhone Duo, assessing its two-screen hardware experience and $2,000 price point [Ars Technica].
- **Indictment in data recovery scam:** The chief executive of MonsterCloud faces criminal charges for allegedly scamming organizations that were actively seeking recovery from ransomware disruptions [Hacker News].
- **Classified US surveillance court ruling withheld:** Reports surfaced that the US government is withholding a secret judicial ruling detailing lawful boundaries around domestic electronic surveillance [Hacker News].
- **Private equity faces $300 billion debt wall:** Financial analysts highlighted that companies backed by private equity are approaching a looming $300 billion debt maturity wall [Hacker News].

## Bangladesh

- **Metro rail expansion agreements finalized:** Bangladeshi authorities signed contracts across four packages to construct 11.5 kilometers of metro tracks and eight new stations [AmaderShomoy.com, Dhaka Mail]. India-based L&T secured the $1 billion contract covering electrical systems, track construction, signaling, and platform doors [The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour].
- **Bilateral investment talks with Japan:** Officials from Japan and Bangladesh engaged in discussions regarding $6.3 billion in private sector financing targeting energy, ICT, and infrastructure [Prothom Alo English]. Japan has also agreed to supply patrol vessels to help secure Bangladesh's maritime borders [Just News BD].
- **Investigation into power grid collapse:** An official inquiry committee was formed to determine the exact factors that caused a recent power grid failure [প্রথম আলো].
- **Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant fuel delivery:** The third consignment of uranium fuel for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant safely reached the project site after transit from Dhaka's international airport [প্রথম আলো].
- **UN report highlights forced military recruitment of Bangladeshis:** A United Nations report stated that Bangladeshi nationals lured abroad with job promises have been coerced into serving in the Russian military in Ukraine [দ্য ডেইলি স্টার বাংলা, ATN News].
- **Home Ministry reaffirms stance against extrajudicial actions:** The Home Minister reiterated the government's strict zero-tolerance policy regarding crossfire incidents, formally distancing administrative policy from controversial remarks made by the Inspector General of Police [প্রথম আলো].
- **Dhaka retail centers face closure pressures:** Longtime retail destination Karnaphuli Garden City ceased operations, while at least 10 other established Dhaka shopping complexes risk closure due to falling foot traffic and shrinking sales [The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour].
- **Appliance manufacturer expands product portfolio:** Haier Bangladesh launched its premium Tigris water heater models alongside its inaugural line of microwave ovens for domestic consumers [The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour].

## Education & Admission

- **High public spending per university graduate:** Official figures indicate the Bangladesh government spends approximately Tk 13.5 lakh per university student each year, even as graduate joblessness stands at 32% [The Daily Campus].
- **Secondary school debate championship:** The sixth annual 'Prothom Alo Bhairab Bondhusava Debate Competition-2026' reached its final stage following rounds among eight secondary school teams supported by local Bhairab administration [প্রথম আলো].
- **Former New Zealand PM joins Sydney faculty:** Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern has officially joined the faculty at the University of Sydney [প্রথম আলো].

---

## Scholarships

- **IWA & Grundfos "Youth Action for SDG 6" Fellowship:** Applications have opened for the 2027–2028 IWA & Grundfos "Youth Action for SDG 6" Fellowship, with an application deadline of November 5, 2026 [Opportunity Desk]. The initiative, established in 2022, provides targeted leadership and professional development support to Young Water Professionals addressing worldwide water sustainability challenges [Opportunity Desk].

## What to watch

- **Riyadh-Dhaka flight resumption:** Saudi Arabian Airlines is expected to resume its direct passenger flights on the Riyadh-Dhaka route following disruptions that impacted over 22,000 travelers across 146 canceled or suspended flights [প্রথম আলো].
- **Dengue preparations ahead of November:** Health authorities in Bangladesh are monitoring seasonal infection patterns and preparing public hospitals for a potential peak in dengue cases during November [Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)].
- **High-stakes international elections:** Observers are monitoring critical voting outcomes occurring across continents, including ongoing national elections in Israel recording high turnout, which carry broad geopolitical consequences [বিবিসি বাংলা, Al Jazeera].
